office.label: Downtown Detroit
office.oneLineDistinction: Corporate, civic and entertainment uses in the central core
office.shortDescription: Downtown Detroit concentrates corporate offices, government, sports, entertainment and hospitality around the riverfront and central business core. Its towers and civic destinations distinguish it from New Center’s institutional corridor and Corktown’s smaller historic commercial blocks.

office.label: New Center
office.oneLineDistinction: Institutional and office buildings around West Grand Boulevard
office.shortDescription: New Center centers on office and institutional buildings around West Grand Boulevard, with a building stock shaped by Detroit’s automotive and civic history. The district is a distinct northern employment node rather than an extension of Downtown or suburban Southfield.

retail.label: Midtown Detroit
retail.oneLineDistinction: Medical, cultural and neighborhood commerce north of Downtown
retail.shortDescription: Midtown Detroit combines medical and university institutions, cultural destinations, offices, restaurants and neighborhood retail north of Downtown. Those anchors produce a mixed institutional and customer-facing district unlike Downtown’s corporate core or Corktown’s lower-scale historic blocks.

retail.label: Corktown
retail.oneLineDistinction: Historic commercial blocks beside mobility-focused redevelopment
retail.shortDescription: Corktown’s historic commercial blocks, restaurants and small businesses sit beside former industrial and rail land now associated with mobility-focused redevelopment. Its compact older fabric and adaptive-reuse opportunities distinguish it from Midtown’s institutional spine.
whatStandsOut: Historic commercial blocks beside mobility-focused redevelopment

industrial.label: Southwest Detroit Industrial
industrial.oneLineDistinction: Heavy industrial and logistics land along the river and rail corridors
industrial.shortDescription: Southwest Detroit contains heavy industrial, manufacturing, logistics and service land tied to river, rail and major road infrastructure. It is a City-of-Detroit operating geography and must not absorb Dearborn, Livonia or other suburban industrial inventory.
whatStandsOut: Heavy industrial and logistics land along the river and rail corridors

industrial.label: Eastern Market
industrial.oneLineDistinction: Food wholesale, production and market activity in a historic district
industrial.shortDescription: Eastern Market combines food wholesaling, production, distribution, public market activity and restaurants in a historic district northeast of Downtown. Its mix of working food businesses and customer-facing market uses creates a specialized Flex context rather than a generic office/warehouse area.
